statutoryAuthority.primary: N.D.C.C. ch. 19-03.1 (controlled substances), first-offense possession sealing provision
statutoryAuthority.ruleStatement: If a person pleads guilty or is found guilty of a first offense involving possession of one ounce or less of marijuana or two grams or less of THC, and judgment is entered, the court, on motion, must seal the court record if the person is not subsequently convicted within two years of a further controlled-substance violation. Once sealed, the court record may not be opened even by court order.
doNotImport: N.D.C.C. ch. 12-60.1 is North Dakota's GENERAL criminal-record sealing chapter. Its three- and five-year clean periods, its clear-and-convincing burden, its forty-five-day hearing floor and its proof-of-service requirement do not govern this route, which is mandatory on motion under ch. 19-03.1. Chapter 12-60.1 is cited in this packet only where the owner-approved manifest itself invokes it by analogy, and it is labelled as an analogy where it appears.

The North Dakota Summary Pardon Application for certain marijuana offenses is a separate remedy administered by the Pardon Advisory Board. It is not this route and its five-year condition must never be applied here.

filingDestination.statement: File the motion in the existing criminal case with the clerk of court.
filingDestination.office: Clerk of court for the court that entered the judgment

feeAndWaiver.statement: No filing fee is identified for this motion. The statewide fee schedule carries no line item for a motion in an existing criminal case.
feeAndWaiver.waiverStatement: A fee waiver application is not included because no fee is identified. If the clerk asks you for a fee, do not pay it before asking which schedule item it is under — this packet was prepared on the basis that none applies.
feeAndWaiver.sourceOfRule: packet-set manifest, participantActionRequired kinds pay_fee and apply_fee_waiver

serviceAndNotice.statement: The subsection states no service requirement, so this packet does not include a certificate of service and does not direct you to serve anyone.
serviceAndNotice.whyNoCertificate: A certificate of service is a required component of a filing packet only where the route requires service. Including one here would assert an obligation the statute does not impose. The absence is deliberate and is recorded so that it reads as a decision rather than an omission.
serviceAndNotice.sourceOfRule: packet-set manifest, participantActionRequired kind serve_party: "None stated by the subsection."

copyRequirements.statement: Bring the original signed motion and the proposed order for the clerk, and keep one complete copy of everything you file for yourself. Ask the clerk whether the court wants an additional copy for the judge — practice varies by district and the statute does not set a number.
copyRequirements.originalPlusCopies: 1 original, 1 participant copy, ask the clerk about a judge's copy
copyRequirements.sourceOfRule: General filing practice. The statute sets no copy count, and this packet says so rather than inventing one.

postFilingTimeline.step: You file the motion and the proposed order with the clerk of court in the existing criminal case.
The clerk dockets the motion in the existing case.
postFilingTimeline.timing: usually the same day or the next business day

postFilingTimeline.step: The court rules on the motion. Sealing under chapter 19-03.1 is mandatory when the conditions are met, so the ordinary outcome is an order granting it.
postFilingTimeline.timing: no statutory deadline applies to the court

postFilingTimeline.step: If the court signs the order, ask the clerk for a conformed copy for your records before the file is sealed.
postFilingTimeline.timing: immediately after the order is signed

hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Chapter 19-03.1 does not require a hearing on this motion. If one is set, attend it and bring the criminal judgment and the charging document.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The prosecutor objects, or the court questions whether this was a first offense or whether the quantity is within the limit.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Those are the two elements of eligibility. If either is disputed, the answer is in the charging document and the criminal history, not in argument.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The court applies chapter 12-60.1's waiting periods or its clear-and-convincing burden to this motion.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: That is the general sealing chapter and it does not govern a chapter 19-03.1 first-offense motion. This is worth raising, and it is worth getting help to raise.
Get the written reason. A denial of relief the statute makes mandatory is a different problem from a denial on the facts.

attachments.title: Criminal judgment
attachments.whyNeeded: It establishes the date judgment of guilt was entered, which is the statutory anchor.

attachments.title: Charging document showing the quantity
attachments.whyNeeded: The quantity charged is an element of eligibility and recollection is not enough.

attachments.conditionDescription: Where the participant is unsure whether any further controlled-substance conviction exists.

participantChecklist.text: Check your answer to "On what date did the court enter the judgment of guilt?" against the criminal judgment, and correct the packet if they disagree.
Check your answer to "What quantity was charged?" against the charging document, and correct the packet if they disagree.
If you are unsure whether you have any further North Dakota controlled-substance conviction, check against your BCI criminal history record and correct the packet if they disagree.
Confirm that this was your first controlled-substance offense. The motion tells the court that it was, and that is one of the things the statute requires.
Sign the motion in the signature block.
No notarization is required for this filing.
No filing fee is identified for this motion, and no waiver application is needed.
